chapters.title: Tobit in Nineveh
chapters.html:
Tobit 1

Tobit and His Tribe

1The book of the words of Tobit son of Tobiel, son of Ananiel, son of Aduel, son of Gabael, of the descendants of Asiel, of the tribe of Naphtali,

2who was taken captive in the days of Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians from Thisbe, which is south of Kedesh of Naphtali in Galilee, above Asher.

3I, Tobit, walked in the ways of truth and righteousness all the days of my life, and I did many acts of charity for my brothers and my nation who had gone with me into captivity to the land of the Assyrians, to Nineveh.

4When I was in my own country, in the land of Israel, while I was still young, the whole tribe of Naphtali my father fell away from the house of Jerusalem, which had been chosen out of all the tribes of Israel for all the tribes to sacrifice there. There the temple, the dwelling of the Most High, was consecrated and built for all generations forever.

5All the tribes that fell away together sacrificed to Baal the heifer, and so did the house of Naphtali my father.

6I alone went often to Jerusalem for the festivals, as it is written for all Israel by an everlasting decree, taking the firstfruits and the tithes of the crops and the first shearings,

7and I gave them to the priests, the sons of Aaron, for the altar. The tenth of all my produce I gave to the sons of Levi who served at Jerusalem. The second tenth I sold, and I went and spent the money in Jerusalem each year.

8The third I gave to those to whom it was due, as Deborah my father's mother had commanded me, for I had been left an orphan by my father.

9When I became a man, I married Anna, a woman of our own family, and by her I had a son, Tobias.

In Nineveh

10When we were carried away captive to Nineveh, all my brothers and those of my race ate the food of the nations,

11but I kept myself from eating it,

12because I remembered God with all my soul.

13The Most High gave me favor and good standing before Shalmaneser, and I became his buyer of supplies.

14I used to go into Media, and once at Rages in Media I left ten talents of silver in trust with Gabael, the brother of Gabrias.

15When Shalmaneser died, Sennacherib his son reigned in his place. His roads became unsafe, and I could no longer go into Media.

16In the days of Shalmaneser I did many acts of charity for my brothers.

17I gave my bread to the hungry and clothing to the naked, and if I saw any of my people dead and thrown out behind the wall of Nineveh, I buried him.

18If King Sennacherib killed any who came fleeing from Judea, I buried them in secret, for in his anger he killed many. When the king looked for the bodies, they could not be found.

19Then one of the men of Nineveh went and informed the king about me, that I was burying them, and I hid. When I learned that I was being sought to be put to death, I was afraid and ran away.

20All my property was seized, and nothing was left to me except Anna my wife and Tobias my son.

21But not fifty days passed before his two sons killed him and fled to the mountains of Ararat. Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place, and he put Ahikar son of Anael, my brother's son, over all the accounts of his kingdom and over all its administration.

22Ahikar spoke for me, and I came back to Nineveh. Ahikar had been cupbearer, keeper of the signet, administrator and treasurer, and Esarhaddon appointed him second to himself. He was my nephew.

Notes

  • v1 "The book of the words of Tobit" — rendered from the Greek, the shorter of its two forms (Swete's main text); the longer Greek is cited where it differs in substance. The names follow the English forms readers know: Greek Enemessar is Shalmaneser (2 Kings 17:3), Sacherdonos is Esarhaddon, and Achiacharus is Ahikar.

  • v3 "acts of charity" — eleēmosynai, from eleos, mercy: mercy shown in what is given. It is the book's word, said of Tobit at the start and taught to his son at the end.

  • v5 "sacrificed to Baal the heifer" — the Greek puts the feminine article before Baal. The longer Greek says plainly to the calf that Jeroboam king of Israel made in Dan (1 Kings 12:28–30).

  • vv6–8 "the firstfruits and the tithes… the second tenth… the third" — three tithes: the Levites' tenth (Numbers 18:21); a second, turned into money and spent in Jerusalem (Deuteronomy 14:22–26); and a third for the guest, the orphan and the widow (14:28–29). Tobit, an orphan himself, gives the third.

  • vv10–12 "I kept myself from eating it" — as Daniel would in Babylon: Daniel resolved that he would not defile himself with the king's food (Daniel 1:8).

  • vv15, 18 "Sennacherib" — the Greek held here reads Acherel, a name found nowhere else. The longer Greek has Sennacherim, and v21 tells his end as Kings tells Sennacherib's: his two sons killed him and fled to the land of Ararat, and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place (2 Kings 19:37).

  • vv17–18 "I buried him" — the act the whole story turns on: Tobit's burying of the dead costs him his goods here and his sight in the next chapter.

  • vv21–22 "Ahikar… my nephew" — the highest official of the Assyrian court is family, and the reason Tobit can come home.

chapters.title: Tobit Blinded
chapters.html:
Tobit 2

The Feast of Weeks

1When I had come home and Anna my wife and Tobias my son had been given back to me, at the festival of Pentecost, which is the holy festival of seven weeks, a good dinner was prepared for me, and I reclined to eat.

2I saw the many dishes, and I said to my son, "Go and bring whatever poor man you find among our brothers who remembers the Lord. I will wait for you."

3He came back and said, "Father, one of our people has been strangled and thrown out in the marketplace."

4Before I had tasted anything, I sprang up and carried him into a room until the sun went down.

5Then I came back, washed myself and ate my bread in sorrow.

6I remembered the prophecy of Amos, how he said, "Your festivals shall be turned into mourning, and all your merrymaking into lamentation."

7I wept. When the sun had gone down, I went and dug a grave and buried him.

8My neighbors laughed at me and said, "He is no longer afraid of being put to death for this. He ran away, and here he is burying the dead again."

The Sparrows

9That same night, after I had buried him, I came back, and because I was unclean I slept by the wall of the courtyard, with my face uncovered.

10I did not know that there were sparrows in the wall. My eyes were open, and the sparrows dropped warm droppings into my eyes, and white films formed on my eyes. I went to physicians, but they did not help me. Ahikar took care of me until he went to Elymais.

Anna and the Goat

11My wife Anna earned money at women's work,

12and she sent it to the owners, and they paid her wages and also gave her a young goat.

13When she came back to me, the goat began to bleat. I said to her, "Where did this kid come from? It was not stolen, was it? Give it back to its owners, for it is not right to eat anything stolen."

14She said, "It was given to me as a gift, besides my wages." But I did not believe her, and I told her to give it back to its owners, and I flushed with anger at her. Then she answered me, "Where are your acts of charity and your righteous deeds? See, everything about you is plain to see."

Notes

  • v1 "the festival of Pentecost, which is the holy festival of seven weeks" — Pentecost, the fiftieth, the Greek name for the Festival of Weeks, kept seven weeks after the harvest began (Deuteronomy 16:9–10).

  • v2 "whatever poor man you find… who remembers the Lord" — Tobit's charity at his own table: the feast is for a guest who is poor and faithful.

  • v6 "Your festivals shall be turned into mourning" — Amos 8:10, I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation. Tobit's feast is turned exactly so.

  • v9 "because I was unclean" — whoever touches a dead body is unclean seven days (Numbers 19:11), so he does not go into the house.

  • v10 "white films formed on my eyes" — leukōmata, white spots, a clouding of the eye. The longer Greek says the droppings brought on the white films. Tobit's blindness comes from his burying of the dead, and the physicians cannot help.

  • v14 "Where are your acts of charity and your righteous deeds?" — Anna turns his own words against him (1:3). The reproach of a wife to a righteous man struck down recalls Job's: Do you still hold fast your integrity? (Job 2:9).

chapters.title: Two Prayers on One Day
chapters.html:
Tobit 3

Tobit's Prayer

1Then in my grief I wept, and in my anguish I prayed, saying,

2"You are righteous, O Lord, and all Your works and all Your ways are mercy and truth, and You judge with true and righteous judgment forever.

3Remember me and look on me. Do not punish me for my sins and for my unknowing errors, and those of my fathers, which they sinned before You.

4For they disobeyed Your commandments, and You gave us over to plunder, to captivity and to death, a byword of reproach among all the nations among whom we have been scattered.

5Now Your many judgments are true in dealing with me for my sins and those of my fathers, because we did not keep Your commandments, for we did not walk in truth before You.

6So now deal with me as it pleases You. Command my spirit to be taken from me, so that I may be released and become earth. It is better for me to die than to live, because I have heard false reproaches, and there is great sorrow in me. Command that I be released from this distress now to the everlasting place. Do not turn Your face away from me."

Sarah in Ecbatana

7On that same day it happened to Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, in Ecbatana of Media, that she also was reproached by her father's maids,

8because she had been given to seven husbands, and Asmodeus the evil demon had killed each of them before they had been with her as with a wife. The maids said to her, "Do you not know that you strangle your husbands? You have already had seven, and you have not had the benefit of one of them.

9Why do you beat us? If they are dead, go with them! May we never see a son or daughter of yours!"

10When she heard these things, she was so grieved that she thought of hanging herself. But she said, "I am my father's only child. If I do this, it will be a disgrace to him, and I will bring his old age down in sorrow to Hades."

Sarah's Prayer

11So she prayed by the window and said, "Blessed are You, O Lord my God, and blessed is Your holy and honored name forever. May all Your works bless You forever.

12And now, O Lord, I have set my eyes and my face toward You.

13Command that I be released from the earth, so that I may no longer hear reproach.

14You know, O Lord, that I am innocent of any sin with a man,

15and that I have not defiled my name or the name of my father in the land of my captivity. I am my father's only child, and he has no child to be his heir, and no near kinsman or son of his to whom I should keep myself as a wife. Already seven husbands of mine have died. Why should I live? But if it does not please You to kill me, command that You look on me and have mercy on me, and that I no longer hear reproach."

Raphael Sent

16The prayer of both was heard before the glory of the great God,

17and Raphael was sent to heal the two of them: to scale away the white films from Tobit's eyes, and to give Sarah the daughter of Raguel as a wife to Tobias the son of Tobit, and to bind Asmodeus the evil demon, because Tobias had the right to inherit her. At that very time Tobit came back and went into his house, and Sarah the daughter of Raguel came down from her upper room.

Notes

  • v2 "all Your ways are mercy and truth" — eleēmosynai, the word of Tobit's own acts of charity (1:3; 2:14). What he gave to his brothers, he names in God.

  • v6 "It is better for me to die than to live" — the prayer of Elijah under the broom tree, Now, LORD, take my life (1 Kings 19:4), and of Jonah, it is better for me to die than to live (Jonah 4:3).

  • v7 "On that same day" — two people in two cities, Nineveh and Ecbatana, pray to die on the same day, and the two stories become one.

  • v10 "I will bring his old age down in sorrow to Hades" — Jacob's words when he would not let Benjamin go: you will bring my gray head down in sorrow to Sheol (Genesis 42:38). Hades is the Greek for Sheol, and Tobit has the words of the Greek Genesis.

  • v11 "she prayed by the window" — as Daniel prayed in his upper room, with its windows open toward Jerusalem (Daniel 6:10).

  • vv16–17 "before the glory of the great God, and Raphael was sent" — the Greek held here reads before the glory of the great Raphael, and was sent; the longer Greek has before the glory of God. The rendering follows the longer Greek for God. Raphael is a Hebrew name, God heals, and he is sent to heal the two.

  • v17 "because Tobias had the right to inherit her" — as the nearest kinsman. The law kept a daughter who inherits within her father's tribe (Numbers 36:8).

chapters.title: Tobit's Charge to His Son
chapters.html:
Tobit 4

"Remember the Lord"

1On that day Tobit remembered the money that he had left in trust with Gabael at Rages in Media,

2and he said to himself, "I have asked for death. Why do I not call my son Tobias and tell him about it before I die?"

3So he called him and said, "My child, when I die, bury me, and do not neglect your mother. Honor her all the days of your life. Do what pleases her, and do not grieve her.

4Remember, my child, that she faced many dangers for you while you were in her womb. When she dies, bury her beside me in one grave.

5My child, remember the Lord our God all your days, and do not set your will to sin or to break His commandments. Do what is right all the days of your life, and do not walk in the ways of wrongdoing.

6For if you act in truth, you will prosper in all your works, as do all who do what is right.

Charity

7Give charity from what you have, and do not let your eye begrudge it when you give. Do not turn your face away from any poor man, and the face of God will not be turned away from you.

8If you have much, give from it in proportion. If you have little, do not be afraid to give according to the little you have.

9So you will be storing up a good treasure for yourself against the day of need.

10For charity delivers from death and keeps one from going into the darkness.

11Charity is a good offering in the sight of the Most High for all who give it.

Marriage and Conduct

12Beware, my child, of all sexual immorality. Above all take a wife from the descendants of your fathers. Do not take a foreign wife, who is not of your father's tribe, for we are the sons of the prophets. Remember, my child, Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, our fathers of old: they all took wives from among their own kindred, and they were blessed in their children, and their descendants will inherit the land.

13So now, my child, love your brothers, and do not in your heart be too proud toward your brothers and the sons and daughters of your people to take a wife for yourself from among them. For in pride there is ruin and much confusion, and in idleness there is loss and great want, for idleness is the mother of famine.

14Do not keep back overnight the wages of any man who works for you, but pay him at once. If you serve God, you will be repaid. Watch yourself, my child, in all that you do, and be disciplined in all your conduct.

15What you hate, do not do to anyone. Do not drink wine to drunkenness, and do not let drunkenness go with you on your way.

16Give of your bread to the hungry and of your clothing to the naked. Give all your surplus as charity, and do not let your eye begrudge it when you give.

17Pour out your bread on the grave of the righteous, but give none to sinners.

18Seek advice from every wise man, and do not despise any useful counsel.

19At all times bless the Lord God, and ask Him that your ways may be made straight and that all your paths and plans may prosper. For no nation has counsel of its own; the Lord Himself gives all good things, and He humbles whom He wills, as He wills. So now, my child, remember my commands, and do not let them be blotted out of your heart.

The Money in Media

20And now I tell you about the ten talents of silver that I left in trust with Gabael son of Gabrias at Rages in Media.

21Do not be afraid, my child, because we have become poor. You have great wealth if you fear God and turn away from all sin and do what is pleasing in His sight."

Notes

  • vv3–4 "Honor her all the days of your life… bury her beside me in one grave" — the commandment, Honor your father and your mother (Exodus 20:12), given its last duty: a grave shared.

  • vv7–11 "charity" — eleēmosynē, the book's word (1:3), five times in five verses. Charity delivers from death (v10) is the proverb, righteousness delivers from death (Proverbs 10:2), with charity where Proverbs has righteousness.

  • v7 "Do not turn your face away from any poor man, and the face of God will not be turned away from you" — a measure for measure: the face turned to the poor is answered by God's face.

  • v12 "for we are the sons of the prophets… Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob" — the fathers are called prophets, and marriage within the family is set beside the blessing of their children. Sarah, the bride the story is preparing, is of Tobit's own kindred (3:17).

  • v14 "Do not keep back overnight the wages" — the law: The wages of a hired man shall not stay with you overnight until morning (Leviticus 19:13).

  • v15 "What you hate, do not do to anyone" — the rule in its negative form. Jesus gives it in its positive form: whatever you want people to do to you, do the same to them (Matthew 7:12).

  • v16 "Give of your bread to the hungry and of your clothing to the naked" — Isaiah's fast: to share your bread with the hungry… when you see the naked, to cover him (Isaiah 58:7). It is what Tobit did (1:17).

  • v17 "Pour out your bread on the grave of the righteous" — the sense is uncertain: perhaps food given to the family of a righteous man who has died, at the meal of mourning.
